sections.html:
Fort Mill is a York County town and a Charlotte suburb, about 646 feet above sea level, with I-77 along its western side. Exit 85 leads to SC Highway 160, the main east-west street. Growth is the story: 10,811 residents in 2010, then 24,521 in 2020, across about 20 square miles after an annexation in 2008 that doubled its size. Easy access to I-77 and SC 160 is part of how many buyers judge a house here.

Founded in 1873, the town has a downtown historic district where Main Street retail sits near Confederate Park and Memorial Park. If your house is in or near that district, ask town planning staff whether any review covers exterior work before you promise a buyer a change.

sections.h2: Is your address really in Fort Mill?
sections.html:
Maybe not. Indian Land lies in neighboring Lancaster County yet shares a Fort Mill mailing address, and Tega Cay is a nearby community in the same school district. A Fort Mill mailing address can come with taxes paid to a different county and permits issued by a different office.

Settle this before you read any tax or permit rule on this page. The York County Assessor or Fort Mill town hall can tell you in one call which jurisdiction holds your parcel.

sections.h2: Weather and the condition of the house
sections.html:
Highs near 90 degrees mark the summer, and winters bring only occasional sleet or snow that rarely sticks. Hurricane Hugo damaged the area badly in 1989. Inspectors usually concentrate on:

  • Roof age and condition after summer storms.
  • Air conditioning age.
  • Tree limbs over the roof, and gutters, on older lots.
  • Any past water intrusion, which belongs on the disclosure form.

York County values and bills the property, and three offices share the work.

OfficePhoneHandles
York County Assessor803-684-8526Values, appraisals, 4 percent legal residence application
York County Auditor803-684-8501Exemptions, tax estimates, millage rates
Tax Collection Office803-684-8527Billed amounts, due dates, payment

State law calls for reappraisal every five years. Ownership is set by the records on December 31 of the prior year, so a deed recorded after that date puts the new owner on the following year's bill. Sellers usually pay their share at closing while the buyer may owe the full-year notice, so settle the split with the closing attorney.

The state sets the ratios: 4 percent for a legal residence and 6 percent for other real property. The first penalty date is January 16. Ask the Tax Collection Office for the schedule and the due date on your bill.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the buyer's tax bill
sections.html:
A sale can trigger a fresh valuation. A property with an assessable transfer of interest is reassessed in the tax year after the transfer, and the 15 percent cap on increases from a countywide reassessment does not apply in the year a qualifying transfer first becomes taxable. Moving a home into a trust also removes the 4 percent assessment until the owner reapplies.

If your escrow payment jumps, the cause may be that the mortgage company estimated taxes at the owner-occupied rate and the owner never applied. The Assessor at 803-684-8526 handles the application.

A South Carolina attorney handles the closing, and the deed is recorded with the York County Register of Deeds. The state Supreme Court treats preparing deeds, examining title and supervising a closing as the practice of law, as discussed in Boone v. Quicken Loans (2017).

The deed recording fee is $1.85 for the first $500 of value plus $1.30 for each further $500, as the Department of Revenue page shows.

Before a contract is signed, a seller must hand the buyer a written property condition disclosure unless an exemption applies. The form asks about water supply and sewer, structural and mechanical systems, wood-destroying insects, zoning and land use, leases, and homeowners association governance. If you live in a subdivision, track down the HOA rules and the current dues before you list, since buyers will ask for both and a missing document slows the deal.

The Town of Fort Mill Building and Codes Department takes permit applications through an online portal called Evolve. You can submit applications, pay fees, check status and schedule inspections there. Call 803-547-2034, or visit Town Hall at 205 N. White Street, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The town enforces the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, the 2021 South Carolina residential and building codes, the 2020 National Electrical Code and the 2021 swimming pool and spa code. Inspection requests in by 3 p.m. are completed the next business day.

If a prior owner finished a basement, added a deck or installed a pool, ask the department whether the permits were closed. Open permits are easier to clear before a sale than during one. For rental or short-term rental questions, ask the town directly if a buyer plans to rent the home.

sections.h2: Commuter buyers and what they want
sections.html:
Many Fort Mill buyers work in Charlotte and weigh a house by its drive to I-77. They also compare the town's newer subdivisions against older homes closer to Main Street. Newer houses sell on layout and finishes. Older ones sell on character, and they raise questions about wiring, plumbing and the roof.

If yours is an older house, a recent roof, updated electrical panel or repaired plumbing are the details to mention first. If something is unfinished, say so plainly. Buyers who find a problem on their own tend to ask for a bigger price cut than buyers who were told about it at the start.

Speed depends on preparation. Pull together your deed or purchase papers, the newest tax bill, HOA documents, permit records and a payoff letter from your lender. Added a basement, deck or pool at some point? Verify its permit status first, because a closed permit is simple proof for the buyer.

A cash buyer generally has no appraisal or lender to wait on, which leaves title work and attorney review as the main timeline drivers. On closing day the attorney retires your loan, takes the tax split out of the proceeds and files the deed.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to if I live in Fort Mill?
faqs.a: Most Fort Mill town addresses are in York County, which bills and collects the tax. Some addresses with a Fort Mill mailing address, such as Indian Land, are in Lancaster County, so check your parcel first.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the 4 percent legal residence rate in York County?
faqs.a: Call the York County Assessor at 803-684-8526. A big jump in an escrow payment can mean the mortgage company estimated taxes at the owner-occupied rate and the owner never applied.

faqs.q: Does selling my Fort Mill house raise the buyer's taxes?
faqs.a: It can. A property with an assessable transfer of interest is reassessed in the tax year after the transfer, and the 15 percent cap on increases does not apply in the year a qualifying transfer first becomes taxable.

faqs.q: Do I need permits to be closed before I sell in Fort Mill?
faqs.a: Open permits are better resolved before closing. Call the Town of Fort Mill Building and Codes Department at 803-547-2034 with your address to find out what is on file.

faqs.q: Can Cash Home Buyers buy a Fort Mill house as is?
faqs.a: We buy houses in any condition, and the closing still runs through a South Carolina attorney and the York County Register of Deeds. Tell us about the property and we will explain what we can do.
